blocks.text: Like its predecessor, Southern Gothic, Midwest Gothic flourishes mainly in literary works. Although most self-described literature in the genre is microfiction on Tumblr, there exists a significant body of literature by established authors that falls into the classification. Some authors known for their Midwest Gothic work include:
More specific stories by authors that more often write outside the genre include:
Something Wicked This Way Comes by Ray Bradbury
Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark series by Alvin Schwartz
After and Before the Lightning by Simon Ortiz
The Roanoke Girls by Amy Engel

A publication worth mentioning in this category is the Midwestern Gothic literary journal, which, though sadly out of print, collected Midwest based fiction, poetry, and nonfiction from various authors.
